posts.text:
The new Rust version of Agent Mail uses the following other libraries and ports that I've made in the last month or so:

FrankenTUI for the console interface
FrankenSQLite
FrankenSearch for message search
FrankenAgentDetection (abstracted out from cass)
Asupersync (zero tokio allowed!) throughout
fastmcp_rust for mcp
sqlmodel_rust for orm
beads_rust for beads integration
toon_rust for token dense payloads

That's what the Flywheel is all about. Making programs and libraries and then turning around and combining them with other new libraries you've made to make still more ambitious new projects.

The reason this project in particular took so long is that I had to first port an ungodly amount of stuff from Python to Rust to make it a truly faithful version of the Python original...

Anyway, I'll probably make an official announcement of it tomorrow or the next day. Don't try to install it yet, it's not actually done! I just wanted to give a sneak peak of what it looks like.
posts.notes: Agent Mail Rust sneak peek — lists all 9 component libraries assembled in the Flywheel manner. Key signal: flywheel composability in action. Official launch imminent. Connects FrankenTUI, FrankenSQLite, FrankenSearch, asupersync, fastmcp_rust, sqlmodel_rust, beads_rust, toon_rust.

posts.text:
Plus:

1) A next-level safe version of SQLite that natively supports multiple concurrent writers using a similar approach to what Postgres uses (this is like 2-3 days from completion already). FrankenSQLite.

2) a from-scratch, radically innovative and safe JS engine and node/bun replacement. FrankenEngine and FrankenNode.

3) next level safe rust versions of Numpy, Scipy, Pandas, NetworkX, Jax, and Pytorch. Faster, better, and all memory safe. Franken<you get the idea>.

4) Same for Redis, Whisper, and Mermaid.

5) FrankenCode (haven't started this yet but it will merge my Rust version of Pi Agent, which is already done, with Codex and my new FrankenEngine and FrankenNode) to make the best, most extensible, and SAFEST agent harness in the world, with the best interface via my FrankenTUI library, which is the best and fastest TUI library in the world now.

6) All of this will flow into FrankenTerm, which is an unholy mixture in Rust of WezTerm, Ghostty, Rio, Zellij, and a ton of my other projects (like process_triage, storage_balast_helper, vibe_cockpit, etc) to make the very best cross-platform terminal emulator with integrated multiplexer that's designed from the ground up to withstand the extreme demands of multi-day sessions involving hundreds of separate agents.
posts.notes: THE FRANKEN ROADMAP. Full 6-item project manifest: FrankenSQLite (concurrent writers Postgres-style), FrankenEngine/FrankenNode (safe JS runtime), safe Rust ports of Numpy/Scipy/Pandas/NetworkX/Jax/Pytorch, Franken Redis/Whisper/Mermaid, FrankenCode (Pi Rust + Codex + FrankenEngine = best agent harness in the world), FrankenTerm (WezTerm+Ghostty+Rio+Zellij cross-platform terminal for hundreds-of-agents multi-day sessions). 66K views, 164 bookmarks. Definitive vision document for the whole Frankenverse.

posts.text:
I developed a pretty advanced, Rust-native, 2-tier lexical/semantic hybrid search system as part of my work on cass and xf and other projects. But rather than repeat myself over and over again, I decided to extract it out into a standalone project called (what else?) FrankenSearch. You can get it here:

https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensearch

I didn't want it to just be a library though, since that limits the appeal to just Rust developers. So I also introduced a reference search implementation called fsfs (FrankenSearch Fast Search) for indexing and searching through your files...

[Full text: embedding model bake-off details, 627mb binary with baked-in semantic models, CPU-optimized, rival to Elastic with less config, screen recording demo.]
posts.notes: FrankenSearch announcement. 2-tier lexical+semantic hybrid search. fsfs CLI reference implementation. Embedding model bake-off in docs. Extracted from cass/xf projects. 154 bookmarks. Potential catalogue tool entry.

posts.text:
Running big agent swarms can be hazardous to your machine's health (pic related).

It has become such a problem for me that I've been forced to create a suite of programs to help me cope with this, including:

1) remote_compilation_helper (rch) for offloading builds to a fleet of dedicated VPS machines (this is the single most critical one).

2) storage_ballast_helper (sbh) for intelligently clearing out junk so you avoid filling up your primary machine or the compilation helper machines.

3) process_triage (pt) for helping to diagnose messed up runaway or zombie processes.

And I've also created various skills for working with all these tools intelligently...

Without these programs, I simply wouldn't be able to work on so many complex Rust projects at the same time.

...these problems are emergent as the number of agents increases, and that seems like the obvious trajectory we're on now.
posts.notes: Agent swarm machine health suite overview: rch (remote compilation offload), sbh (storage ballast), pt (process triage). Key insight: these problems are emergent at scale with many agents. Strong operational signal for multi-agent infra practitioners.

Then I'm going to port Pi agent to Rust. Once I have that, I'm going to try to combine the best elements of the Rust Pi agent with codex, but using FrankenTUI for console rendering and my asupersync library for all networking and file IO.

I'm calling it FrankenCode, and I'm pretty excited about it. It's going to be spectacular, like some kind of alien artifact.
